text:
Sara: heads-up — APAC support ticket: some iOS users on IPv6-only carrier networks get 503s for /v1/generate. Repro via TestFlight+carrier sim.
Priya: that points at NAT64/DNS64 issues or LB dualstack mismatch. which endpoint is affected? api.prod or regional edge?
Ethan: tested from a sydney jumpbox, dig shows AAAA for api.prod.redwood.ai in ap-southeast:
```
$ dig +short AAAA api.prod.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
2604:...:1a2b
```
but curl from an IPv6-only emulator times out/returns 503.
Alex: infra-bot flagged a spike: ALB target-group ap-southeast-backends had 3/6 unhealthy.
infra-bot: ALERT: ap-southeast-1 alb healthcheck failures — /health 502 for 3 targets (since 2026-03-17T02:14Z)
Devon: quick repro from local ipv6 stack (using provider NAT64):
```
$ curl -6 -v https://api.prod.redwood.ai/v1/generate
* Connected to api.prod.redwood.ai (64:ff9b::c0a8:1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 handshake...
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
```
Sara: tcpdump on the node shows SYN then RST from backend 10.0.2.5 shortly after handshake. no obvious app crash.
Priya: two possibilities: 1) backend ingress/firewall blocks NAT64 translation addresses, 2) ALB healthchecks originate over IPv4 and target group config isn't dualstack-safe, confusing routing.
Ethan: logs show reject "client_ip_not_allowed" in kube-authz, and the source ip is one of our NAT64 egress boxes (10.10.200.14). We didn't include NAT64 boxes in the allowlist.
Alex: so IPv6 client -> NAT64 translation -> NAT64 egress IP -> hits backend. If that IP is blocked, the request will be refused even though DNS resolution was fine.
Devon: short-term options:
- add our NAT64 egress pool IPs to backend allowlists (fast)
- create synthetic A records for api.prod.redwood.ai for APAC zones so IPv6-only clients fall back to IPv4 resolver behaviour (provider-dependent)
- enable DNS64 on provider edge (if available)
- ensure ALB/ingress is configured for dualstack target groups and healthchecks

Costs/ops: spin up managed NAT64 instances (one per AZ) adds baseline infra + EIP costs. Synthetic A is cheap but brittle and needs maintenance for failover.
Priya: cost estimate: small NAT64 fleet across 3 AZs ~= $150/mo + ips + NAT throughput perf testing. Synthetic A per region negligible cost but requires pinning IPs and more DNS rules.
Sara: immediate mitigation: add NAT64 egress IPs to allowlist and create synthetic A for ap-southeast zone for a canary subset of traffic (10% via split-horizon). That should stop the 503s tonight.
Ethan: will open RW-INFRA ticket and PR to add allowlist entries + conditional DNS change. I'll also add a kube iptables rule audit to avoid similar surprises.
Alex: long term we should: enable true dualstack on LB/ingress, remove app-level allowlists that assume client-ip is public IPv4, and test NAT64 path in CI.
Devon: test commands we used (put these in the ticket):
```
# reproduce DNS
dig +short AAAA api.prod.redwood.ai
# emulate nat64 path
curl -6 -v https://api.prod.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# tcpdump filter
sudo tcpdump -nni any host 10.0.2.5 and tcp
```
infra-bot: Created task RW-INFRA-4523: "APAC IPv6-only NAT64 client failures - add NAT64 egress allowlist & synthetic A canary" and assigned to Ethan, Priya. ETA: canary tonight.
Sara: thanks — please post rollout notes in #incidents when changes going live. :thumbsup:
Priya: will do. I'll also follow up with Product so Support has a KB entry for IPv6-only carriers.
